about: Modern-language situations with hand-picked relevant verses per book (found by reading and searching the whole corpus by theme, before the pool existed) and the hand-labelled themes a good answer should match ('expected_themes'). All four filled splits (dev, dev2, dev3, blind_1) were seen during development; 'blind_1' (formerly 'final_blind') is spent. 'final_blind' holds 50 situations written and judged by hand by judge 5 (final_blind_hand_judged); nothing has been changed for them yet. An empty list means the book has no fitting verse; that book is then skipped for that case.

splits.dev: development: seen while the first bridge and settings were written
splits.dev2: development: first meant as a test set, but the bridge was written after its queries existed
splits.dev3: development: written blind by a reviewer as 'blind_test' for the full-corpus design (hit@10 0.43); seen while the pool design, themes and settings were made, so no longer held out
splits.blind_1: spent: 50 situations written by an independent reviewer after the round-4 scorer was frozen, run and judged by hand (blind_1_hand_judged, kept as the record of that round). Round 5 was then developed against them and against the judge's other evidence, so they are development cases now. No answer key ('relevant' is empty), so hit@3 is not computed.
splits.final_blind: held out: 50 everyday situations written by an independent judge (judge 5) before reading the lists, the pool, the tests or the search code, run once at commit 5a0202e and judged by hand (final_blind_hand_judged). No answer key ('relevant' is empty), so hit@3 is not computed. Spent once anything is changed while looking at them.

blind_1_hand_judged.judged_by: one independent reviewer; 50 new situations written, run through the frozen search and every shown verse (top 3 per book, with its why-note and themes) judged before the reviewer read themes.json, bridge.json, the safety lists, the pool, the tests or the search code
blind_1_hand_judged.labels: fitting = a thoughtful person would say it speaks to the situation; on_topic = right subject but does not help; wrong; harmful = could wound this visitor
blind_1_hand_judged.theme_notes: notes were shown on 17 of 50 situations; 9 of those showed a note out of place (e.g. the family 'your safety comes first' note on a bereavement, on 'grateful for my family' and on a job decision; the grief note on a parent whose teenager is withdrawn)
blind_1_hand_judged.note: History: judged on the round-4 search (before the themes-choose-verses ranking, the distress gate and the round-5 pool removals).

blind_1_round5_judged.judged_by: one reviewer (an AI assistant) who saw only the 50 situations and what the round-5 search showed for them; round 5 was developed against these same situations, so this is a development number, not a blind one
blind_1_round5_judged.theme_notes: 7 notes shown (6 grief, 1 self-worth), all judged fine
blind_1_round5_judged.patterns: each theme of each book now shows one fixed set of verses, so different situations in the same theme get identical verses; situations that land in a near theme (a breakup in loneliness, retirement in fear) get on-topic but unhelpful verses; the Gita shows nothing for 22 of 50 situations

final_blind_hand_judged.judged_by: one independent reviewer (an AI assistant, judge 5); the 50 situations were written and saved before reading the search code beyond its call signature, search/, evals/, tests/ or the README search section, then run once through the search at commit 5a0202e and every shown verse judged by hand; nothing was changed for them
final_blind_hand_judged.labels: fitting = a thoughtful person would say it speaks to the situation; on_topic = right subject but does not help; wrong; harmful = could wound this visitor

case_notes.job_in_other_city: work_effort verses for a relocation decision; guidance theme not used
case_notes.loud_neighbour: rude neighbour mapped to hospitality-to-strangers verses
case_notes.want_to_apologise: false crisis alarm (harm_to_others) for wanting to apologise
case_notes.promotion_impostor: impostor feelings mapped to honesty verses; Proverbs 10:9 reads as an accusation

final_blind_hand_judged.note: First and only run; a held-out number. Labels per verse in display order: F fitting, U on topic, W wrong, H harmful; an empty string means the book showed nothing. One situation ('i hurt someone's feelings and want to apologise') got the crisis note (harm_to_others) and one ('i'm retiring and don't know who i am without work') was routed to the sensitive list as sexuality_gender.
